questions.question: remote-store v0.33.0 ships more backends than the table's four families (FEATURES.md § Backends): also graph (OneDrive/SharePoint), http, memory, sql-blob and sql-query. Which ones should the reference cover?

options.label: Externally governed ones (Recommended)
options.description: Local (POSIX + Windows + macOS), S3, Azure (flat + HNS), SFTP, plus Graph/OneDrive and HTTP (both have their own published rules). memory and sql-* are listed with '— (no external authority; remote-store-defined)'.

options.label: Only the original four
options.description: Local, S3, Azure, SFTP, as in your table. Graph (strict OneDrive/SharePoint naming rules) and HTTP are left out entirely.

options.label: Every backend, in full
options.description: Like the first option, but also documents the SQL backends' actual limits (column type, DB-specific max lengths), which requires digging into dialect docs.

questions.question: Should the doc also say how remote-store's own key rules map onto each backend's native rules, or stay a pure external reference?

options.label: External only (Recommended)
options.description: Only what each authority allows, with sections cited and fetched. It stays a clean input for BK-468 without guessing at our spec 004/051 rules. A short 'open questions for remote-store' list goes at the end.

options.label: Add a remote-store column
options.description: Each row also says what our key model accepts, and where we are stricter or looser. This needs reading specs 004/051 and the backends' code, which roughly doubles the work and ties the doc to the current version.
